name: Marcus Manilius
bio: Marcus Manilius was a Roman poet of the late Augustan or early Tiberian age. Nothing is known of his life beyond what his one surviving poem reveals: he wrote after the death of Augustus, which the poem alludes to, and his birthplace and station are unrecorded.

His Astronomica, an unfinished didactic poem in five books of hexameters, is the earliest surviving systematic treatment of astrology in Latin. It describes the heavens and the zodiac and teaches how the stars bear on human lives, and it was rediscovered in the Renaissance, when A. E. Housman later edited it in five volumes.
